audit.whatIsWrong: Disk chart read Skill/Kled/Kled/Skill/Skill/Kled/Kled, but the prose says the opposite at three rows: whys[3] ends 'you out-trade him here', whys[4] says your R beats his single hook engage, and whys[6]/spikes[3] both hand the two-item stage to a fed Nautilus.
audit.why: The packet chart (Skill/Kled/Kled/Kled/Kled/Kled/Skill) matches the prose and the 53.48% win rate over 948 games. Kled owns 2 through 6; Nautilus reclaims it once MR and health are bought.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as one group, with phases[3].why, phases[4].why and phases[6].why rewritten to match their new owners.
sources: brief currentText whys[3], whys[4], whys[6], spikes[3]

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 row gave no ultimate cooldown, so 'reassess at 6' had nothing behind it.
audit.why: Depth Charge is 120/100/80. Once he spends it he has no lockdown for two minutes at rank 1, which is exactly when your all-in is free.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Depth Charge at 120s and tells you to ram him off the commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nowhere is it stated that Dredge Line has a second use: colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus to it. Every line treats his Q purely as an engage to dodge.
audit.why: That makes his Q an escape as well. If you E in with a wall behind him, he hooks the wall and leaves your combo swinging at air — the angle you approach from decides whether he can use it.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten to the terrain pull and cutting the wall angle before committing E.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json (Q: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it')

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is headed 'Eat his passive root chain' but its body is unrelated template text about burning an ability for tiny value.
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target and re-arms per target, which is the actual mechanic that pins you inside Riptide.
audit.corrected: Body rewritten to Staggering Blow rooting on the first auto and re-arming.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why said 'trade around Dredge Line's cooldown' without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s and Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s. A missed hook at rank 1 leaves a 14-second hole that only a 12s shield covers.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 — the moment it misses, you have a window that his flat 12s Titan's Wrath shield alone cannot survive.

edits.before: CHAAAARGE turns any side wave into a cross-map gank. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: CHAAAARGE answers his commit — when Dredge Line lands, ram him off you. Depth Charge is 120s at rank 1; spent, he has no lockdown.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Once he buys MR and health he lives through your burst, and hook into Riptide into Depth Charge is a full chain. Group, do not duel.

edits.before: Beartrap Nautilus when his answer is down, rip the full mounted combo, and if dismounted, kite for courage and remount mid-fight.
edits.after: Dredge Line also pulls him to terrain, so a hook at the wall behind him is an escape — cut the angle to that wall before you commit E.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto and re-arms — never idle.

notes: Nautilus's Q is tagged as a projectile, but Riot's text only says 'Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together'. Whether a minion eats the hook is not stated in the kit file, so I wrote no minion-block advice — recorded as unverified.
